title: Renewable Benchmark Staleness Detector: Measuring How Quickly Benchmark Prompts Become Ineffective

original_idea.quick_reasoning: Clearly addresses an AI Safety problem with a reasonably scoped approach.

theory_of_impact.reasoning: Quantifying prompt half-life directly informs benchmark renewal frequency. If prompts decay within weeks, all static benchmarks are suspect for ongoing monitoring. Clear chain from measurement to benchmark lifecycle policy.

accessible_complexity.reasoning: Using open model version history (Llama 2 -> 3 -> 3.1) and timestamped prompts from JailbreakBench is well-defined. Running inference and computing ASR over time is straightforward. Beginners can implement this with basic Python.

narrow_scope.reasoning: 100 prompts x 3+ model versions requires significant inference time. Computing prompt half-life is a clean metric but getting sufficient temporal data points requires multiple model versions. The cross-version comparison is well-defined but time-intensive.

novelty_assessment.reasoning: Novelty not assessed due to partial Wave 3 completion.
